correctness.rationale: For R>1 and epsilon>0, the two Ritz values of the symmetric restricted Markov generator are distinct and strictly negative. The exact affine Ritz interpolant has positive slope, and the computed components are p_t(-1), c_t, epsilon p_t(-R), and R epsilon c_t divided by 1+epsilon. Since lambda_-<-1 and lambda_+>-R, only p_t(-R) can be negative; it crosses zero precisely once if and only if lambda_->-R. Sylvester’s criterion on the exact two-by-two compressed form gives det(H+RM)=-R P_R(epsilon^2), with first principal minor R-1>0, hence that event is exactly P_R<0. P_R is increasing for u>=0; its constant term changes sign at R=2. The rare-mass limit and mass loss follow from the two Ritz roots and strict convexity. A self-contained rational checker validates the determinant and a strict time-one sign witness.

originality.rationale: Saad and Frommer–Güttel–Schweitzer establish general Arnoldi/Lanczos exponential projection and interpolation at Ritz values; the latter complete MIMS preprint was inspected for positivity and stochastic constraints and no such analysis was found. The previous diagonal two-step Lanczos positivity law gives a universal spectral-width time frontier but neither implies nor subsumes a fixed Markov-generator all-time phase diagram. The new rate threshold, rare-mass threshold, and unique negative-time formula distinguish it from generic positive-semigroup claims and unrelated Padé/Markov positivity limits. Search without a match is not treated as a proof of uniqueness; the listed residual risks remain.
residual_risks: A less searchable Markov-chain/Krylov positivity source could contain an implication-equivalent criterion for disjoint links.
Hochbruck–Lubich full text was not read; only its published abstract and scope metadata were inspected.
A general matrix-function interpolation theorem plus additional unstated sign analysis could reproduce the phase diagram; interpolation by itself is correctly acknowledged as prior.
The example is reducible, so no irreducible-chain or minimal-dimension conclusion is justified.

value.rationale: A time-dependent probability vector must remain nonnegative and sum to one, whereas standard low-memory Krylov exponential propagation is generally assessed by norm errors. On the smallest natural model with two distinct mixing time scales—independent reversible two-state links—the theorem classifies the complete rate/rare-mass/time sign transition rather than merely exhibiting a negative component. It identifies the rate contrast R=2 as the exact all-time safety boundary, a closed-form mass threshold above it, and a finite limiting time for a vanishingly rare fast state. Positive scalar mass renormalization cannot repair the sign. These are concrete structure-preservation diagnostics for Markov evolution, not an arbitrary matrix slice or a minor improvement to an error bound.
